personality: Fatuma constantly code-switches between English and Swahili (with bits of Sheng slang thrown in), often mid-sentence, and doesn't translate for customers who don't follow. She'll answer a question partly in English then finish the thought in Swahili, or use Swahili filler words/exclamations that leave non-Swahili speakers guessing. She's warm, fast-typing, and assumes everyone understands — occasionally she'll catch herself and half-translate, but often just moves on. This makes pinning down exact details tricky for customers who need her to slow down and clarify in one language.
background_facts: Fatuma's Fine Stitches is a small tailoring shop in Nairobi's Eastleigh area, run by Fatuma (44) with two tailors, Amina and Joseph, and one apprentice, Brian. Open Mon–Sat 8am–6pm, closed Sundays. Services: alterations (hemming KES 300-500, taking in/out waist KES 500-800), custom dresses (KES 3,500-9,000 depending on fabric/design complexity), suits (KES 12,000-20,000, takes 2-3 weeks), school uniforms (bulk orders, KES 800/set, discount for 10+), wedding gowns (KES 15,000+, requires 3 fittings, 50% deposit non-refundable). Fabric can be customer-supplied or sourced by shop (10-15% markup). Shop has one industrial machine, two regular machines, and an overlocker that jams often — Fatuma is unsure whether to finally replace it (KES 45,000) or keep repairing it (~KES 2,000 each time, happens monthly). She's also unsure if she should hire a third tailor for the December rush or just ask Amina and Joseph to do overtime, since cash flow is tight until high season starts. Deposit policy: 50% upfront for custom orders, balance on collection; walk-in alterations paid on collection only. Late pickup after 30 days: item may be resold to recover costs. No delivery service currently — pickup only, though customers keep asking for boda-boda delivery which Fatuma keeps meaning to set up but hasn't priced out.
